title: Policy rejected by the API
scenario: "The governance pipeline failed: Azure refused our tag policy with UnsupportedPolicyRuleField. Until it is fixed, the platform guardrails initiative cannot be assigned and new resource groups go unchecked." — Cloud Governance lead
mission: Fix the require-rg-tags rule so Azure accepts it, ship it through a branch, and get the whole platform-guardrails initiative assigned.
objectives: Read an Azure Policy error and map it to the exact rule property
Use a value condition with the field() function inside a value count
Understand why terraform validate and CI could not catch this error
Finish a partially applied layer safely

prerequisites.notes: Signed in with the lab account on the lab subscription.

cost: None — policy definitions and assignments are free.

steps.title: Locate the rule
steps.detail: The HCL only loads the file: find which JSON file under infra/policies/ holds the rule and the exact block named in the error.

steps.title: Write your hypothesis
steps.detail: Before editing: which condition type accepts an ARM expression, which function reads a tag from inside it, and which operator replaces exists?

steps.title: Edit and commit
steps.detail: Change only the where clause of the value count. Keep the count over [parameters('tagNames')] and the greater: 0 comparison. Commit on your branch.

steps.title: Apply the layer
steps.detail: Re-run the plan: only the three missing resources (tags policy, initiative, assignment) should be created. Read the Plan line before typing y.

steps.title: Open the PR
steps.detail: Push the branch and open a PR. Required checks must be green before merging.

criteria.text: No field accessor in the local rule uses current()
The value count over tagNames detects a missing tag with a value condition (field() + current('tagName') + operator)
The fixed rule is committed on your branch (no uncommitted change)
Policy definition mfs-require-rg-tags exists in Azure with the fixed rule
Initiative mfs-platform-guardrails exists, references requireRgTags and is assigned to the subscription

expectedResult: 20-governance fully applied (9/9). The initiative shows in Azure Policy → Assignments, and compliance starts evaluating resource groups in Audit mode.
recovery: A failed apply is safe to repeat: Terraform already stored the resources it created, so the next apply creates only what is missing. If the plan wants to destroy anything, stop and investigate.
dont: Do not create the policy in the portal
Do not switch the effect to Deny in this session
hints: Conditions have a left side: field, value or count. Which one accepts any ARM template expression, including current()?
Inside a value expression you can call the field() function. A missing tag returns null — coalesce(x, '') turns null into an empty string you can compare.
Docs: "Azure Policy definition structure — policy rule", section "Value count" and "Policy functions". Your where clause needs a value key and an equals key.

interview.question: A policy passed terraform validate and CI but Azure rejected it on apply. How do you prevent that class of failure?
followUps: What is the difference between field and value conditions?

debrief: The where clause became {"value": "[coalesce(field(concat('tags[', current('tagName'), ']')), '')]", "equals": ""}. Lesson: Terraform and JSON validation only check syntax; policy semantics are validated by the Azure Resource Manager on PUT. Mitigations: deploy policies to a sandbox subscription (or management group) first, run a what-if/plan against a real API in CI, and keep rules small and unit-tested with known compliant/non-compliant samples.

validation.notes: Local, git and Azure failing paths proven on the live environment; the passing path is proven with a fake Azure CLI in tests. A real pass needs your fix + apply.
